1.explanation:
The key logic that (a) decides when to apply “auto-stretch” to a single image on a RevealJS slide and (b) that collects and re-injects <aside> blocks into the slide lives in format-reveal.ts. In particular:

• applyStretch(doc, autoStretch) in format-reveal.ts is stretching the image to fill the entire slide section, without accounting for the height of any aside element at the bottom. It needs to be updated so that, when an aside exists, the image’s maximum height is computed as slideHeight – asideHeight.  

• revealHtmlPostprocessor (also in format-reveal.ts) is collecting up <aside> elements and appending them after the stretched image, thereby layering the aside on top of the image’s lower portion (or caption). It must be reordered or adjusted so that the aside reservations are applied before stretching, or the image container is resized accordingly.

The kAutoStretch constant (in constants.ts) is what toggles this behavior on or off; it may also need to be consulted (or made slide-specific) so that the stretch filter can detect and respect aside elements. By fixing the logic in these two files, the stretch calculation can be bounded by the aside’s footprint and the overlap will be eliminated.
1.bug_scenario:
On RevealJS slides that include exactly one figure plus an “aside” block at the bottom, the image is being stretched all the way to the bottom of the slide, then the aside is rendered on top of it (and even on top of the figure caption, when one exists), resulting in overlap. The desired behavior is that the aside always owns the bottom region of the slide and that the single figure should only stretch to the top of the aside block (leaving the aside’s space clear).

In the screenshots you can see:
- Slide 1 (no caption): the kitten image is stretched so far down that the aside text overlays the bottom of the image.
- Slide 2 (with caption): the caption is pushed below the aside because the aside is laid on top of the stretched image and its caption.
